IDT12420.text:

IDT12420.synoptic: A high pressure system over the Bight extends a ridge over Tasmania before a cold front moves across the state during the day on Friday, followed by a cold southwesterly wind flow which will persist on Saturday. Another high pressure system moves close to Tasmania on Sunday, drifting southeast from Monday.

IDT12326.name: South East Coast
IDT12326.text:
Thursday 5 November
Winds: West to southwesterly 20 to 30 knots turning northwesterly in the evening.
Seas: 2 to 3 metres.
Swell: West to southwesterly 1 to 1.5 metres inshore, increasing to 2 to 2.5 metres offshore.
Weather: Partly cloudy.

Friday 6 November
Winds: Northwesterly 20 to 30 knots tending westerly in the morning then decreasing to 15 to 25 knots in the evening.
Seas: 1.5 to 2.5 metres.
Swell: West to southwesterly 2 to 3 metres inshore, increasing to 3 to 4 metres offshore during the morning.
Weather: Cloudy. 95% chance of showers, with possible small hail in the afternoon and evening.

Saturday 7 November
Winds: West to southwesterly 15 to 20 knots tending south to southwesterly 15 to 25 knots during the day.
Seas: 1.5 to 2 metres.
Swell: Southwesterly 2 to 3 metres inshore, increasing to 3 to 4 metres offshore.
Weather: Partly cloudy. 90% chance of showers, with possible small hail.

Sunday 8 November
Winds: South to southwesterly 15 to 20 knots turning southeasterly 10 to 15 knots during the afternoon.
Seas: 1 to 1.5 metres, decreasing to 1 metre during the afternoon.
Swell: Southwesterly 2 to 3 metres inshore, increasing to 3 to 4 metres offshore.
Weather: Cloudy. 50% chance of showers.
